compensating.why: hop 1 finds the title elements with a selector query instead of the tag lookup
hop 2 reads the element's own text instead of its combined text
hop 3 trims the text before handing it on as well as after

ownership_reason:
Only the gold decides how whitespace is written; hop 1 only queries the document's title elements, hop 2 picks the first and reads its text ("" when there is none), hop 3 trims the ends of what hop 4 returns, and hop 4 passes the text along. The gold's javadoc promises the text with its whitespace normalised in the same way as the text of an Element, which "Hello there       now" is not. No one-line change above the gold that keeps to the hops' documentation restores the trigger: more trimming leaves the interior whitespace, ownText() of a whitespace-preserving title is the same raw text, and select("title") finds the same element. The convention is pinned outside the gold: StringUtil.normaliseWhitespace writes a run of whitespace as one space (StringUtilTest normaliseWhiteSpace: "   hello    
  there    
" -> " hello there "), TextNode.text returns 'normalised text' through it, and Element.text normalises the text of an element and its children (ElementTest testNormalisesText: "Hello There. Here is some text." from text with ' 
 ' runs); the facade's own javadoc ('Trimmed title') is unchanged.
